mail.welcome.title: About Your Mailbox
mail.welcome.body: @,^Lewis here. I've taken the liberty of adding a small almanac to your mailbox.^You'll get a note at the turn of each season, and a short one a week in. Nothing official - just the festivals worth clearing your day for, a few things I've watched farmers forget, and a warning before the season turns.^The notes come round again every year, so don't feel obliged to keep them.^ -Mayor Lewis
mail.SpringOpen.title: Spring Has Started
mail.SpringOpen.body: @,^Spring again. The ground is soft and everything is possible, which is a dangerous combination.^Two festivals this season: the Egg Festival on the 13th, and the Flower Dance on the 24th.^One piece of advice I give every farmer: plant something on the first dry day, even if it's only a row. Spring is shorter than it feels, and the harvest you skip in week one is the one you miss in week four.^ -Lewis
mail.SpringMid.title: Five Days To The Egg Festival
mail.SpringMid.body: Dear @,^The Egg Festival is on the 13th, in the town square. There's an egg hunt, and the prize is worth the walk.^If you plan on the Flower Dance on the 24th, start asking early - nobody agrees to dance with a stranger, and a gift the day before helps more than a gift on the day.^The season's seeds are cheapest right now, before the greenhouse crowd buys them all up.^ -Evelyn
mail.SpringClose.title: Last Night Of Spring
mail.SpringClose.body: @,^Tomorrow the season turns.^Anything still in the ground that isn't a spring crop will be gone by morning, so harvest what you want to keep before you sleep tonight.^While you're out there: empty the machines, clear the shipping bin, and walk the fence line. Summer is busy, and repairs are cheaper now than they'll be then.^ -Robin
mail.SummerOpen.title: Summer Is Here
mail.SummerOpen.body: @,^Summer. The water's warm, the fish are biting, and the sun will not let up.^Festivals: the Luau on the 11th, and the Dance of the Moonlight Jellies on the 28th.^Something I'd tell any farmer: water early, before the heat, and keep a little energy in reserve. You'll want it at the beach.^ -Willy
mail.SummerMid.title: Three Days To The Luau
mail.SummerMid.body: Hello @,^The Luau is on the 11th, down at the beach.^Bring something for the soup pot. The Governor tastes it in front of everyone, and the whole town remembers how it turned out - good or bad. A fresh, high quality ingredient never hurts.^If you'd rather stay home and work, that's a choice too. Just don't tell Gus I said so.^ -Gus
mail.SummerClose.title: Last Night Of Summer
mail.SummerClose.body: @,^The jellies come tonight, and tomorrow it's fall.^Harvest everything you're keeping, empty the kegs and jars, and check the sprinklers - the ones that survived summer will probably survive fall too.^Fall is the season that pays, so have your seed money ready before the shop opens.^ -Pierre
mail.FallOpen.title: Fall, And The Fair
mail.FallOpen.body: @,^Fall. This is the season that pays for the rest of the year, so don't lose the first week to tidying up.^Festivals: the Stardew Valley Fair on the 16th, and Spirit's Eve on the 27th.^One thing worth knowing: fall crops are worth more than what you planted in spring, and they take about as long. Spend your seed money here, not in winter.^ -Pierre
mail.FallMid.title: Grange Display Reminder
mail.FallMid.body: @,^The Stardew Valley Fair is on the 16th.^If you're entering the grange display, you can show up to nine items. The judging is generous with variety - a vegetable, a fruit, a fish, a forage item, an artisan good and a mineral will score better than nine pumpkins.^Also: the star tokens you win there buy things you can't get anywhere else.^ -Lewis
mail.FallClose.title: Last Night Of Fall
mail.FallClose.body: @,^Last day of fall.^Harvest everything you mean to keep - winter kills whatever is left in the ground. Then do the winter jobs while it's still cheap: hay in the silo, fences repaired, animals settled.^They'll stay indoors once the snow comes. They'll be fine, as long as the silo is full.^ -Marnie
mail.WinterOpen.title: Winter Work
mail.WinterOpen.body: @,^Winter. Nothing grows outside now, and that isn't the disaster it looks like - it's the season for the work you can't do in the sun.^The mines are quiet, the fishing is good, and the ice gives up more than you'd expect.^Festival of Ice on the 8th, the Night Market from the 15th, and the Feast of the Winter Star on the 25th.^ -Clint
mail.WinterMid.title: Night Market And The Feast
mail.WinterMid.body: @,^Three things coming, in order.^The Night Market opens on the 15th and runs three nights - it stays open late, and it's the one place you can buy things the shops never carry.^Then the Feast of the Winter Star on the 25th. You'll get a letter naming your secret gift recipient; keep an eye out for it, and don't leave the shopping to the morning of.^ -Evelyn
mail.WinterClose.title: Last Night Of Winter
mail.WinterClose.body: @,^Tomorrow the snow stops and the year starts over.^If you've been meaning to clear the farm, tonight is the last quiet night for it - spring arrives with more to do than you remember, and the first dry day is worth more than the whole of winter.^I'll be up on the mountain, as always. Come by when the weather turns.^ -Linus
